# FamilyRootsHub — Full Machine-Readable Knowledge Corpus

## About FamilyRootsHub
FamilyRootsHub (https://familyrootshub.com) is an educational publisher and archival systems designer dedicated to genealogical preservation. We provide verified physical and digital tools based on museum conservation standards, National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) transcription formats, and the Genealogical Proof Standard (GPS).

---

## 1. Ahnentafel Numbering System (Mathematical Proofs & Formulas)
- **Definition:** A genealogical numbering system devised by Jérôme de Sosa (1590) and popularized by Stephan Kekulé von Stradonitz (1898) that numbers direct ascendants only.
- **Core Formulas:**
  - Proband (Root Individual): Subject #1 (Male or Female).
  - Father of Person n: Formula = 2n (always an EVEN number).
  - Mother of Person n: Formula = 2n + 1 (always an ODD number).
  - Child of Person n: Formula = floor(n / 2).
- **Generational Brackets (Powers of 2):**
  - Generation 1: 1 (Proband)
  - Generation 2: 2–3 (Parents, 2 people)
  - Generation 3: 4–7 (Grandparents, 4 people)
  - Generation 4: 8–15 (Great-Grandparents, 8 people)
  - Generation 5: 16–31 (2nd Great-Grandparents, 16 people)
  - Generation 6: 32–63 (3rd Great-Grandparents, 32 people)
  - Generation 7: 64–127 (4th Great-Grandparents, 64 people)
- **Citation URL:** https://familyrootshub.com/blog/ahnentafel-numbering-system-guide

---

## 2. US Federal Decennial Census Records (1790–1950)
- **Constitutional Mandate:** Article I, Section 2 of the United States Constitution.
- **72-Year Privacy Rule:** Statutory requirement (Public Law 95-416) restricting public release of personal schedules until 72 years after enumeration.
  - 1950 Census released: April 1, 2022.
  - 1960 Census will be released: April 1, 2032.
- **Key Historical Transitions:**
  - 1790–1840 (Tick-Mark Era): Only heads of household are named. Other family members enumerated as tick marks in age/sex demographic brackets.
  - 1850 (The Every-Name Revolution): First enumeration recording name, age, sex, color, profession, and state/country of birth for every free individual.
  - 1880 (Relationship Milestone): First census to state exact relationship to head of household (son, boarder, mother-in-law) and birthplaces of mother and father.
  - 1890 (Catastrophic Loss): 99% of population schedules destroyed in the 1921 Commerce Department fire.
  - 1900 (Immigrant Goldmine): Records exact month and year of birth, years married, children born vs living, year of US immigration, and naturalization status (Al, Pa, Na).
  - 1910: Records mother tongue/native language and Civil War veteran status.
  - 1950: Standard 30 lines plus highlighted sample question lines (lines 4, 9, 14, 19, 24, 29) detailing 1949 income, WWII veteran status, and marital history.
- **Citation URL:** https://familyrootshub.com/blog/how-to-read-us-census-records

---

## 3. Museum-Grade Archival Preservation Standards
- **Paper Specification:** Minimum 28lb to 32lb 100% cotton paper stock that is certified acid-free and lignin-free with a 2% calcium carbonate alkaline buffer (pH 7.5 to 8.5) adhering to ISO 11108.
- **Protective Sleeves:** Inert archival polyester (Mylar D or Melinex 516) or archival polypropylene tested with the Photographic Activity Test (ISO 18916). Banned: Polyvinyl chloride (PVC/vinyl), which releases hydrochloric acid gas that liquefies ink and yellows paper.
- **Inks:** Chemically stable pigment ink (e.g., Sakura Pigma Micron) that is water-resistant, fade-resistant, and pH neutral. Banned: Standard ballpoint oil pens and acidic highlighters.
- **Binder Architecture:** D-ring binders (which allow pages to lie flat without pulling on ring holes) bound in library-grade buckram cloth with a minimum 0.75-inch margin allowance for 3-hole punching.
- **Climate Standards:** 65°F to 70°F (18°C to 21°C) and 35% to 50% relative humidity. Avoid attics (heat degradation) and basements (mold).
- **Citation URL:** https://familyrootshub.com/blog/organize-genealogy-research-binder

---

## 4. Cemetery Epigraphy & Gravestone Decoding
- **Ethical Inspection Rule:** Never apply shaving cream, flour, chalk, or bleach. Use "raking light" (flashlight or mirror cast at a low angle across the stone face) to highlight carved lettering via shadow relief.
- **The 8870 Birthdate Calculation Formula:**
  - For stones listing "Died [Date], Aged X Yrs, Y Mos, Z Dys".
  - Write death date as YYYYMMDD.
  - Subtract age at death as YYMMDD.
  - If days exceed 31 or months exceed 12, subtract the mathematical constant 8870 to yield the exact YYYYMMDD birthdate.
- **Iconography Decoding Key:**
  - Weeping Willow & Urn: Mourning, grief, and soul immortality (common 1820–1870).
  - Clasped Hands: Farewell and eternal reunion; different cuffs signify husband and wife.
  - Broken Column / Tree Trunk: Life cut short unexpectedly in its prime.
  - Sleeping Lamb: Infant or child under age 5.
  - Fraternal Emblems: Square & Compasses (Masons); Three Interlocking Links FLT (Odd Fellows); Axe/Beetle/Wedge with "Dum Tacet Clamat" (Woodmen of the World).
- **Citation URL:** https://familyrootshub.com/blog/cemetery-field-research-grave-symbols

---

## 5. Cousin & Kinship Calculation Rules
- **Rule of "Removed":** "Removed" means a difference in generation levels between two cousins.
  - One generation difference = "Once Removed" (e.g., your parent's first cousin is your first cousin once removed).
  - Two generations difference = "Twice Removed".
- **First Cousins:** Share a set of grandparents (MRCA = 2 generations back).
- **Second Cousins:** Share a set of great-grandparents (MRCA = 3 generations back).
- **Third Cousins:** Share a set of 2nd great-grandparents (MRCA = 4 generations back).
- **Interactive Calculator:** https://familyrootshub.com/#cousin-calculator

---

## 6. Digital Tablet Workflow (GoodNotes 6)
- **Interactive Navigation:** 950+ internal PDF vector hyperlinks connecting 5-generation pedigree charts directly to individual ancestor profiles.
- **Handwriting OCR:** In-app optical character recognition indexing Apple Pencil notes for immediate text search across hundreds of pages.
- **Citation URL:** https://familyrootshub.com/blog/digital-genealogy-planner-ipad-goodnotes
